entries.045f65edc78cd816: This is a business that operates 'Rawang Memorial Park' in Malaysia. The securities report states that the business remained solid against the backdrop of increased demand for suburban cemeteries and columbaria accompanying soaring urban land prices, and gives revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 as ¥894 million (down 0.9% from the previous year) and operating profit as ¥101 million (down 28.7% from the previous year). Revenue from cemetery plot sales is recognized at the point in time when the property is delivered under the sales contract.

entries.79ac6db7f5cabf66: A reportable segment that includes the rental of stores, parking lots, and the like and the supply of hot spring water, real estate development such as housing, the development and management of cemeteries, and investment in financial instruments. For the fiscal year ended December 2025, sales were ¥946 million (down 8.8% from the previous fiscal year) and operating profit was ¥137 million (down 47.9% from the previous fiscal year). Sales are centered on the cemetery business in Malaysia, for which the securities report gives sales of ¥894 million. The securities report explains this segment in its description of business by dividing it into 4 categories, but amounts are stated separately only for the cemetery business and the securities investment business.

entries.d7cb1f757db9c909: This is the central reportable segment of the company group, which operates hotels and ryokan. The securities report lists five facilities that the company operates and manages: 'Hotel Agora Osaka Moriguchi', 'Hotel Agora Regency Osaka Sakai' and 'Dorsett by Agora Osaka Sakai' in Osaka Prefecture, and 'Agora Place Tokyo Asakusa' and 'Agora Tokyo Ginza' in Tokyo; it lists 'Agora Kyoto Karasuma' and 'Agora Kyoto Shijo' in Kyoto Prefecture and 'TSUKI' in Tokyo as facilities it operates under contract. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥8,962 million (up 22.1% from the previous year), and segment profit was ¥1,395 million (up 99.7% from the previous year). The securities report states that, against the backdrop of the weaker yen, the number of foreign visitors to Japan increased (42,683,600 for the full year 2025), and that this drove its performance. In particular, in the Osaka area, the number of guests at 'Hotel Agora Regency Osaka Sakai' and 'Hotel Agora Osaka Moriguchi' increased substantially due to higher demand for accommodation accompanying the Osaka-Kansai Expo. 'Dorsett by Agora Osaka Sakai' opened in March 2025, and 'Agora Place Osaka Namba' ended its operations at the end of July 2025.
